_note: License / language / last update / input / layout / output are from the survey table the user supplied (2026-10-17). 'recipe' is the Yosys script or command each tool uses by default, taken from that tool's own source or README, so every tool is run the way it runs for its users.

ours.name: rtl2diagram (ours) — elk
ours.why: Detailed level: best mean rank on x2's system-view designs (2.67 of 6), and the same ELK layered algorithm netlistsvg / d3-hwschematic / DigitalJS use, so it is the like-for-like comparison.
ours.draws: Block diagram: named functional units and the buses between them, ELK layered layout.

ours.name: rtl2diagram (ours) — busbar
ours.why: Paper-figure level: beats hola on both designs (picosoc 2 vs 3 crossings; darksocv ranked 1st of 6 overall).
ours.draws: Block diagram in paper-figure style: the same units, shared buses drawn as bars.

run.name: netlistsvg
run.draws: Cell-level schematic of the top module: every gate, mux and constant; submodules as plain boxes.

minimal.none: Its only shrinking switches are skin flags (constants / splitsAndJoins off). They delete connections (picosoc loses 20, darksocv 31) and tie unrelated constant inputs together, so they lose information rather than abstract. CLI flags are only -o, --skin and --layout; its README's other Yosys scripts (prep -flatten, aigmap) add detail.

run.name: Yosys show
run.recipe: yosys: read_verilog -sv <files>; prep -top <top>; show -format dot -prefix <out> <top>  →  dot -Tsvg
run.draws: Cell-level graph of the top module (RTLIL cells and wires); submodules as boxes.

minimal.option: show with a selection: submodule cells of the top plus their wires
minimal.effect: Only the submodule instances and the wires touching them; all glue logic, constants and splices dropped.
minimal.evidence: yosys -h show: show [options] [selection], -notitle, -wireshape; yosys -h select: %C (cells of module type), %i, %x1.
minimal.caveats: Nets that pass through glue logic (e.g. picosoc's iomem/irq muxing) appear as dangling named wires. show itself has no black-box mode; the reduction comes from its documented selection argument.

module_minimal.none: Its top-level option selects submodule instances, and a leaf has none; the default prep + show is already its coarse, unflattened view.

run.name: Yosys viz
run.recipe: yosys: read_verilog -sv <files>; prep -top <top>; viz -format dot -prefix <out> <top>  →  dot -Tsvg
run.draws: Signal-group graph. With default options the whole top module collapses into one group that lists its wires.

minimal.option: viz -6, clock/reset excluded (-x), inter-instance wires as one group (-G)
minimal.effect: Instances as separate blocks with the wires between them; glue logic and clock/reset left out.
minimal.recipe: prep -top <top>; select -set inst <top>/t:* <top>/t:$* %d <top>/t:$paramod* %u; viz -format dot -6 -x w:<clk> -x w:<rst> -G @inst %co1 @inst %ci1 %i <top>/w:* %i . @inst @inst %x1 %u  →  dot -Tsvg
minimal.evidence: yosys -h viz (-0..-9 effort, -x exclude, -G user group) and yosys -h select (t:, %d, %u, %co, %ci, %x) in Yosys 0.70+145; viz has no black-box switch of its own, the block view comes from its documented selection argument.

per_design.picosoc: 1 node → 8 nodes / 7 edges (default merged the whole top into one group)

minimal.caveats: The reviewer found this recipe; it is smaller than the researcher's (9/10 and 11/13). viz never prints instance names or cell types, so blocks are only identifiable by the wires listed in them.

module_minimal.option: Most merged effort that still splits the module (-x clock/reset)
module_minimal.recipe: prep -top <top>; viz -format dot -<N> -x w:<clk> -x w:<rst> <top>, with N the highest of 9..0 that gives more than one group (spimemio_xfer: -6, darkuart: -9)  →  dot -Tsvg
module_minimal.effect: Signal groups of the module; clock and reset left out.

run.name: d3-hwschematic
run.recipe: yosys (examples/verilog_to_json.sh): hierarchy -top <top>; synth -run coarse -noabc -noalumacc -nordff; splice; write_json -compat-int  →  d3.HwSchematic.fromYosys → bindData, headless Chromium
run.deviation: Added write_json -compat-int. Without it, today's Yosys writes parameters as binary strings and the importer throws 'Incorrect width00000000000000000000000000000001' (getPortNameSplice).
run.note: hwtGraph is not used: it converts HWT (Python) designs, not Verilog. d3-hwschematic's own Yosys importer is the Verilog path.
run.draws: Cell-level schematic after coarse synthesis; submodules as collapsible boxes.

minimal.effect: One box for the top module with its ports; submodules were already collapsed by the importer.
minimal.recipe: same Yosys script as before (… splice; write_json -compat-int) → fromYosys → rename the top node's children/edges to _children/_edges → bindData
minimal.evidence: README.md, LNode: "If the children should be collapsed by default, the children `children` and `edges` property should be renamed to `_children` and `_edges`"; src/yosys.js already does this for submodules.
minimal.caveats: Expanded or collapsed is the only control: no expand depth, no way to hide logic cells while keeping the submodule boxes, so the minimal view jumps straight to a single box (like a symbol).

module_minimal.none: Its only control is collapsing a node; collapsing the leaf would leave a single box with ports, not a structure. The default draws the coarse cells.

run.name: DigitalJS + yosys2digitaljs
run.recipe: yosys2digitaljs (its default Yosys script) → digitaljs.Circuit.displayOn, headless Chromium
run.draws: Gate-level circuit of the top module, ready to simulate; submodules as boxes.

minimal.effect: Same gate-level circuit with constants, inverters and mux chains folded into fewer devices.
minimal.recipe: yosys2digitaljs as before → json = digitaljs.transform.transformCircuit(json) → new digitaljs.Circuit(json).displayOn(...)
minimal.evidence: digitaljs src/index.mjs:19 exports transform; src/transform.mjs:448 transformCircuit; ChangeLog.md:62 "Circuit graph transformations, which make common circuits generated by Yosys more readable"; digitaljs_online's "Simplify diagram" checkbox (on by default) calls it.
minimal.caveats: Still a cell-level netlist. --optimize (opt -full) helps picosoc a little more but makes darksocv bigger; techmap/abc options fail in yosys2digitaljs 0.10.3 and would add detail anyway; dagre layout only straightens wires; subcircuits are already collapsed.

run.name: sphinxcontrib-hdl-diagrams (yosys-blackbox)
run.recipe: .. hdl-diagram:: <all files concatenated> :type: yosys-blackbox :module: <top>  (prep -top; cd; show)
run.draws: Same as Yosys show, produced inside a Sphinx documentation build.

minimal.none: :type: yosys-aig and :flatten: both add detail; :yosys_script: is a free-form hook that runs any Yosys script, not a simplification the extension offers.

run.name: sphinxcontrib-hdl-diagrams (netlistsvg)
run.recipe: .. hdl-diagram:: <all files concatenated> :type: netlistsvg :module: <top>  (prep -top; cd; write_json -compat-int → netlistsvg)
run.draws: Same as netlistsvg, produced inside a Sphinx documentation build.

minimal.none: Its :skin: option could only pass netlistsvg's lossy constants / splitsAndJoins flags (see netlistsvg); :flatten: adds detail.

run.name: Symbolator
run.draws: Only the top module's port symbol; no internals.

minimal.none: It only ever draws the top's port symbol, which is already its most abstract view; --no-type only removes pin-type text.

run.name: TerosHDL schematic
run.recipe: yosys (colibri/yosys/yosys.ts): read_verilog -sv <each file>; hierarchy -top <top>; proc; write_json  →  normalizeNetlist → TerosTechnology/netlistsvg#hierarchy render(default.svg, hierarchy.enable=all, expandLevel=0)
run.draws: Cell-level schematic with every submodule expanded inline (whole design on one sheet).

minimal.effect: Top level only: submodules stay boxes with named ports instead of being expanded inline.
minimal.recipe: yosys: read_verilog -sv <each file>; hierarchy -top <top>; proc; opt; write_json  →  netlistsvg fork with hierarchy.enable "off" (rest of the extension's config unchanged)
minimal.evidence: teros-netlistsvg lib/ConfigModel.ts:7 (enable: off|level|all|modules), lib/FlatModule.ts:64-100, lib/config.json:3 (default "off"), README.md:211-239; opt goes in the extension's "Arguments passed to Yosys" setting (config_web.ts:1866-1871, inserted at yosys.ts:87).
minimal.caveats: A VS Code user can type opt, but cannot pick "off": schematic.ts:356-370 hard-codes "all" and the viewer has no setting for it. "off" is the fork's own default and is documented in its README. Top-level glue logic (muxes, comparators, constants) is still drawn.

module_minimal.recipe: yosys: read_verilog -sv <file>; hierarchy -top <top>; proc; opt; write_json → netlistsvg fork with hierarchy.enable "off"

run.name: Digital-IDE
run.version: 0.4.6 (2025-07-09). The current 0.5.0 package on the Marketplace ships all 102 netlist-viewer files (netloom, avoid.wasm, yosys.wasm, index.html) as 0-byte placeholders, so it cannot render.
run.recipe: yosys (out/function/dide-netlist/worker.js, mode 'before'): read_verilog -sv -formal -overwrite <files>; design -reset-vlog; proc; write_json  →  resources/dide-netlist/view in headless Chromium
run.draws: Cell-level schematic of the top module with its own symbol set; submodules as boxes.

minimal.none: Its one knob, schema-mode before / after / RTL, picks the Yosys script, not a detail level ('after' is byte-identical, 'RTL' is larger); submodules are already black boxes. darksocv still fails in every mode: darkspi.v instantiates a missing spi_master and the viewer reads that cell's port_directions.

run.name: Verilator vl_hier_graph
run.deviation: Added -Wno-fatal (picosoc leaves picorv32 pins unconnected, which Verilator treats as fatal lint) and -Gdpi=72 when rendering SVG (the script sets dpi=300 for raster output, which shrinks an SVG drawing into one corner).
run.note: Module hierarchy only (which module instantiates which), no nets. CréVinn is a published method, not a runnable tool; this is its runnable Verilator part.
run.draws: Module hierarchy only: which module instantiates which, no signals.

minimal.none: It already draws only the module hierarchy and has no detail, depth or filter options; the rest of its arguments pass through to Verilator.
